summary_paragraph: A 59-year-old woman with advanced HIV (CD4 22, high viral load), end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and a history of post-herpetic neuralgia was admitted for a painful, swollen, and infected femoral dialysis catheter site. She was found to have MRSA bacteremia and catheter-related infection, prompting removal of the infected catheter and initiation of intravenous vancomycin. A new catheter was placed in the right femoral vein, but a transesophageal echocardiogram revealed it had traversed an undiagnosed atrial septal defect into the left atrium, with a small transient thrombus at the tip. The catheter was replaced with a shorter one to prevent recurrence. During admission, she developed C. difficile colitis, likely due to antibiotic exposure, and was treated with metronidazole. She restarted antiretroviral therapy and was discharged home on a three-week course of vancomycin with dialysis, oral metronidazole, and a new HIV regimen, with close follow-up planned.
